## Continuation Wave 12 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 12 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a blue flag on a hinge, a stone cup on a wall, a shallow print beside a culvert, and a lamp turned toward the shelter**. Observable markers include **flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance**.

### Pass 122 — Blue Flag Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a blue flag on a hinge, a stone cup on a wall, a shallow print beside a culvert, and a lamp turned toward the shelter become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a blue flag on a hinge, a stone cup on a wall, a shallow print beside a culvert, and a lamp turned toward the shelter as physical evidence and flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises flag visibility, cup position, print age, alert fatigue, shelter coverage, and return distance at their boundary values.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Blue Flag Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 13 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 13 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a yellow pennant on a rail, a cup balanced on a post, a line of disturbed dust, and a lantern pointed toward the road**. Observable markers include **pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth**.

### Pass 133 — Yellow Pennant Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a yellow pennant on a rail, a cup balanced on a post, a line of disturbed dust, and a lantern pointed toward the road become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a yellow pennant on a rail, a cup balanced on a post, a line of disturbed dust, and a lantern pointed toward the road as physical evidence and pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises pennant visibility, cup balance, dust age, alert fatigue, road reach, and return depth at their boundary values.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Yellow Pennant Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 15 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 15 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a green cord on a latch, a cup beneath a gutter, a line of stones across a path, and a shutter aimed at the flats**. Observable markers include **cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve**.

### Pass 155 — Green Cord Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a green cord on a latch, a cup beneath a gutter, a line of stones across a path, and a shutter aimed at the flats become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a green cord on a latch, a cup beneath a gutter, a line of stones across a path, and a shutter aimed at the flats as physical evidence and cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises cord visibility, gutter cup level, stone line age, alert fatigue, flatland reach, and return reserve at their boundary values.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Green Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

It crosses at least three current domains and gives the player verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, and return actions. Quiet success protects a routine; costly success spends a real resource; refusal preserves the prior state; unresolved play records a visible unknown. The host projects source, age, confidence, and next action with keyboard/controller parity, readable localization, non-color cues, and safe empty, stale, redacted, and error states. Durable results use the current save owner; derived summaries rebuild on restore. A same-seed fixture repeats ordered inputs after save, reload, duplicate delivery, interruption, and content correction. The receipt records validator evidence, migration defaults, allocation and event-fan-out budgets, rollback, and the stop line.

## Continuation Wave 16 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 16 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a black cord across a post, a cup inside a drainpipe, a fan of leaves beside a track, and a shutter angled toward the marsh**. Observable markers include **cord contrast, pipe cup depth, leaf fan age, alert fatigue, marsh reach, and return footing**.

Treat the visible markers cord contrast, pipe cup depth, leaf fan age, alert fatigue, marsh reach, and return footing as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

## Continuation Wave 17 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 17 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a silver cord at a gate, a cup on a stone sill, a crescent of pebbles by a ditch, and a shutter turned toward the scrub**. Observable markers include **cord sheen, sill cup level, pebble crescent age, alert fatigue, scrub reach, and return anchor**.

### Pass 177 — Silver Cord Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord sheen, sill cup level, pebble crescent age, alert fatigue, scrub reach, and return anchor as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Silver Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord sheen, sill cup level, pebble crescent age, alert fatigue, scrub reach, and return anchor with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Silver Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a silver cord at a gate, a cup on a stone sill, a crescent of pebbles by a ditch, and a shutter turned toward the scrub become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Silver Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 18 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 18 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry**. Observable markers include **cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold**.

### Pass 188 — Copper Cord Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry as physical evidence and cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold at their boundary values.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Copper Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry as physical evidence and cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold at their boundary values.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Latch Loop Repair Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 20 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 20 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a brass cord over a latch, a cup in a wall recess, a fan of pine needles beside a path, and a shutter facing the basin**. Observable markers include **cord shine, recess cup level, needle fan age, alert fatigue, basin reach, and return span**.

### Pass 210 — Brass Cord Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord shine, recess cup level, needle fan age, alert fatigue, basin reach, and return span as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Brass Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord shine, recess cup level, needle fan age, alert fatigue, basin reach, and return span with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Brass Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a brass cord over a latch, a cup in a wall recess, a fan of pine needles beside a path, and a shutter facing the basin become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Brass Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Brass Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present cord shine, recess cup level, needle fan age, alert fatigue, basin reach, and return span with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Brass Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a brass cord over a latch, a cup in a wall recess, a fan of pine needles beside a path, and a shutter facing the basin as physical evidence and cord shine, recess cup level, needle fan age, alert fatigue, basin reach, and return span as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. ## Continuation Wave 21 — Plan 10 — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

Wave 21 adds a new owner-bound layer for **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. Material anchors include **a steel cord tied to a rail, a cup on a ledge above a culvert, a fan of dry grass beside a marker, and a shutter facing the flats**. Observable markers include **cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach**.

### Pass 221 — Steel Cord Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners; it does not mint a second perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response ledger. Treat the visible markers cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a steel cord tied to a rail, a cup on a ledge above a culvert, a fan of dry grass beside a marker, and a shutter facing the flats become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a steel cord tied to a rail, a cup on a ledge above a culvert, a fan of dry grass beside a marker, and a shutter facing the flats as physical evidence and cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises cord edge, ledge cup level, grass fan age, alert fatigue, flat reach, and return reach at their boundary values.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Steel Cord Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 22 high-volume field bank — Perimeter Watch, Threat Signals, and Safe Response

This compact bank expands **perimeter watch, threat signals, and safe response** through the existing **security, combat, wildlife, weather, expedition, radio, roster, and shelter operations owners**. It remains authored scaffolding: each row has a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source, lifecycle, localization key, owner, and rollback note. Samples exercise **cord gleam, ledge cup level, shell scatter age, alert fatigue, quarry reach, and return threshold** against **a copper cord looped through a latch, a cup on a drain ledge, a scatter of shells along a path, and a shutter facing the quarry**, and high-volume expansion stops when reachability, persistence, or deterministic ordering is unproven.

### High-volume field 1 — Iron cord families

The **iron cord families** field covers **watch, source, contact, direction, signal, refusal**. Start with a validated sample, reject duplicate IDs and unresolved references, and mark each value as authored data, a projection, or durable owner state. Include verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, and return routes with quiet, costly, refused, and unresolved outcomes.
